title: Stage 6 — Wire Frontend & Backend
goal: Connect your UI to the SQLite API with fetch, CORS, and professional debugging tools.
summary: Postman and the Network tab first — then fetch, CORS, and loading/error states. The full stack finally talks.

pages.title: Test the API with Postman or curl
fetch and JSON in the browser
CORS — why the browser blocks you
Loading and error states in the UI

checkpoint.prompt: Before wiring fetch in the browser, why test with Postman or curl first?

choices.text: Proves the API works without CORS or UI bugs in the way
Postman replaces the need for an API

checkpoint.explanation: Isolate layers: if Postman succeeds but the browser fails, the bug is in the frontend or CORS — not the handler.

checkpoint.prompt: Network tab shows status 404 for GET /workouts. Where do you look first?

choices.text: The API route and database — the server returned 404

checkpoint.explanation: 404 means the server responded. Check the route path, handler logic, and whether a row exists.

checkpoint.prompt: After `const res = await fetch(url)`, how do you get JSON?
Frontend :5500, API :3001 — browser blocks fetch with a CORS error. Likely fix?

choices.text: Enable CORS on the API for the frontend origin
Merge both into one port by deleting the API

checkpoint.explanation: Different ports = different origins. The API must allow the frontend.

checkpoint.prompt: While fetch is in flight, the user should see…

choices.text: A loading indicator — not a blank screen or stale data
Nothing — wait silently with no feedback

checkpoint.explanation: Professional UIs show loading, success, empty, and error states explicitly.

checklist.label: GET and POST tested with Postman or curl before browser wiring
Frontend uses fetch instead of local mock array
CORS configured so browser requests succeed
UI shows loading while fetch is in progress
UI shows a clear message when fetch fails

questions.prompt: Why test the API with Postman before debugging fetch in the browser?

choices.text: Separates API bugs from CORS and frontend bugs
Postman is required to run Express
fetch only works after Postman approves the route

questions.explanation: Postman/curl hit the server directly — no browser security layer in the way.

questions.prompt: What does the Network tab show for each fetch call?

choices.text: URL, method, status code, headers, and response body
Only CSS rules applied to the page

questions.explanation: Network is your X-ray for HTTP — compare what the browser sent with what the API returned.

questions.prompt: After `const res = await fetch(url)`, how do you get JSON?
Frontend on :5500, API on :3001 — fetch blocked by CORS. Why?

choices.text: Different ports are different origins; the browser enforces cross-origin rules
GET requests are forbidden in JavaScript

questions.explanation: The API must send CORS headers allowing your frontend origin.

questions.prompt: A data-fetching view should handle which states?
questions.explanation: Users need feedback at every step — not a blank screen while waiting or after failure.
